title: Cardinal Labs - weekly pilot results & network/kernel debrief
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on networking anomalies (MTU/fragmentation), a small throughput regression after kernel 2.1 quant build, and next-step validation tests. SE and NetOps agreed on a golden-path egress test, a controlled MTU rollback on two hosts, and a telemetry patch to capture KV cache miss counts. Security asked for a short KMS handshake timeline and proof-of-concept SOC2 artifact before pilot expansion.
topics: MTU mismatch and packet fragmentation causing increased latency/kv cache misses
Kernel 2.1 quantized runtime regression and mitigation options
Golden-path synthetic workload for deterministic validation
VPC egress rules and gRPC keepalive tuning
KMS handshake timeline and compliance artifacts request
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Raman (Redwood); Mark Talbot, Sara Liu, Kevin Ortiz (Cardinal Labs)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i see we have the usual crew. Quick agenda, we want to triage the MTU issue, go over the kernel 2.1 regressed path results, and decide next steps for validation. mark, you want to kick off with the network readout?

[00:25] Mark Talbot: yeah thanks alex. So this morning we saw a bump in tail latency spiking around 95th for the private cluster, basically correlates with fragments and reassembly on the firewall. we're running 1500 MTU on the host but some of the path devices are 1400 after an edge update, so chunking is happening. that increases token latency and we suspect kv cache misses because small TCP packets break the fast path.

[01:12] Priya Raman: can you say the observed kv miss delta? i remember the telemetry was noisy last week.

[01:19] Mark Talbot: nominal miss rate is ~0.8% but during the spike it jumped to 6.4% for a 10-minute window, on a subset of nodes. sara has a more detailed breakdown.

[01:34] Sara Liu: yep, i pulled the traces — it's not universal, it's isolated to the edge subnets that traverse the third-party transit. packet reassembly stalls the steady batching so the runtime falls back to single-token latency. also noticed a slight increase in retransmits.

[01:54] Alex Chen: ok that matches what priya saw in the KV timeline; when reassembly happens, the continuous batching scheduler loses alignment. Two immediate mitigations: enforce MTU 1400 on hosts to match path or enable jumbo frames end-to-end. which is easier for you?

[02:12] Mark Talbot: ops preference is to downgrade host MTU on the two affected racks — less invasive. we'll try a staged rollback tonight.

[02:25] Priya Raman: we'll provide a short playbook for rollback and a script to validate no packet loss post-change — golden-path checks. also include a perf-run to capture tokens/sec and kv hit rate.

[02:41] Sara Liu: sounds good. question: will that impact encryption offload or any tunnel MTU? we use ipsec for egress to the partner transit.

[02:49] Alex Chen: good call — priya, can you add ipsec/path MTU checks into the script? i think we should verify both UDP and TCP paths.

[03:05] Priya Raman: yes. i'll add icmp mtu probes and a gRPC small-payload test to ensure keepalives behave.

[03:20] Mark Talbot: also, we saw a throughput regression after the kernel 2.1 quantized runtime was applied last week. throughput fell ~12% for 4k token sequences, and p95 latency rose 18%.

[03:38] Alex Chen: right, we noticed that in the canary too. priya — what do logs show for kernel-side scheduling and vectorized kernels? any obvious slowdown?

[03:48] Priya Raman: the 2.1 kernel swapped a new matmul path optimized for int8 but it triggers a suboptimal memory layout for sequences above 2k in our current build. that increases copies and invalidates a couple of prefetch heuristics. it's fixable: either roll back the kernel shim, use the previous matmul fallback, or apply a patch to adjust tile size heuristics.

[04:10] Kevin Ortiz: from security, any rollback need a risk blurb? we can't just flip kernels in prod without a quick verification and approvals.

[04:19] Alex Chen: totally — we'll treat it like a patch release. Priya, can you draft a small risk/rollback note and a test checklist?

[04:28] Priya Raman: yes, i'll prepare a one-pager: scope, risk, smoke tests (latency, tokens/sec, kv hit rate), and a canary window.

[04:36] Mark Talbot: timeline wise, we want to run the MTU rollback tonight, then a controlled kernel rollback tomorrow morning if needed. that keeps the impact windows separated.

[04:47] Sara Liu: when you say kernel rollback, do you mean the runtime shim on the inference nodes or a full host kernel bump?

[04:55] Priya Raman: runtime shim — it's a user-space change layered on top of the inference runtime, not the Linux kernel. sorry for ambiguity earlier.

[05:03] Mark Talbot: ok that makes it safer.

[05:08] Alex Chen: great. Next, telemetry: we need to capture KV cache eviction/miss counts correlated with packet-level drops. current traces don't tie them together.

[05:19] Priya Raman: i'll ship a telemetry patch that adds a tag to the token timeline when a fragment is detected and increments a KV-miss counter. that'll let us correlate in datadog.

[05:29] Sara Liu: can that be toggled via config so we don't increase overhead outside the test windows?

[05:33] Priya Raman: yes, feature flaggable. default off, enable per-node.

[05:39] Kevin Ortiz: on the compliance front, we need a short note for KMS handshake timing — our legal wants RTO/RPO for key retrievals and the audit logs. any impact from the runtime change?

[05:50] Alex Chen: the runtime change doesn't touch KMS calls, but the private deployment handshake and the HSM rotations are part of the pilot. we'll send the KMS timeline and the relevant SOC2 artifacts.

[06:02] Kevin Ortiz: perfect, please include encryption at rest certs and key rotation cadence.

[06:10] Priya Raman: will do, i'll attach the KMS handshake doc and a small timing experiment plan.

[06:16] Mark Talbot: quick Q about fallback routing — if we see repeated KV miss spikes, can we auto-fallback to a compatible hosted variant temporarily?

[06:26] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood can route per policy — we can create a canary route that sends 5% traffic to hosted fallback with a different quantization profile. but that requires agreement on data residency and policy.

[06:39] Kevin Ortiz: that's a big data residency ask. hosted fallback needs to be cleared through compliance first, can't be automatic for regulated data.

[06:48] Alex Chen: understood; we'll keep fallback as manual for now.

[06:53] Priya Raman: operationally, for the golden-path synthetic, we'll run a deterministic prompt set that exercises long-sequence attention and KV reuse. results should include tokens/sec, p50/p95, and kv hit rates. we'll provide the harness repo link in the meeting notes.

[07:10] Sara Liu: can you also include an eBPF sidecar suggestion? we've seen success using eBPF for fast packet inspection without touching the host net stack.

[07:19] Priya Raman: noted. i'll include an eBPF optional probe in the harness — low overhead, only enabled on canary nodes.

[07:28] Mark Talbot: another note: we saw gRPC keepalive timeouts at scale; connection churn exacerbates batching issues. any quick tuning you recommend?

[07:36] Alex Chen: increase keepalive to 60s and tune the max concurrent streams — priya, can you provide recommended settings for our runtime, and a short howto for the firewall team?

[07:44] Priya Raman: yes, i'll add recommended gRPC keepalive and max stream settings, plus a script to validate with conntrack.

[07:52] Mark Talbot: thanks.

[08:00] Alex Chen: okay let's move to decisions and actions. We've got three primary actions: MTU rollback tonight on two racks, telemetry patch and golden-path harness to run after rollback, and kernel shim rollback plan if throughput doesn't recover.

[08:17] Kevin Ortiz: Security would like the SOC2 excerpt and encryption proof in one business day.

[08:23] Alex Chen: we can get that out within 24 hours. priya, can you confirm distribution?

[08:28] Priya Raman: yep — i'll attach to the ticket and share with kevin and legal.

[08:32] Mark Talbot: on the MTU test, we'll schedule the change at 23:00 local, 2-hour maintenance window, canary on rack A then rack B.

[08:42] Sara Liu: we'll monitor with enhanced telemetry and slack alerting to the #pilot-ops channel.

[08:47] Alex Chen: perfect. Any blockers or other open questions?

[08:52] Sara Liu: none from ops. Just one small ask — include a sanity test for the ipsec endpoints post-mtu change.

[08:58] Priya Raman: already in the check script.

[09:02] Mark Talbot: thanks.

[09:06] Alex Chen: cool. Quick recap: MTU rollback tonight, telemetry patch + golden harness, kernel shim rollback plan ready tomorrow morning, KMS/SOC2 artifacts within 24 hours, no automatic hosted fallback for now. We'll follow up with links and a proposed timeline in the ticket.

[09:28] (end)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and minor word swaps typical of auto-transcripts.
